strings.manage/noPorts: No container publishes a port on this host.

strings.editor/iconHint: A web path relative to the ArozOS root, or an image URL.
strings.editor/pathDesc: On this address: {path}. Nothing to set up.
strings.editor/subdomainDesc: On its own host name, e.g. app.example.com. Isolated from ArozOS.
strings.editor/pathWarn: In path mode the app shares the ArozOS address. Its web pages can act as the signed in user on ArozOS, so only use it for software you trust. Choose subdomain mode for anything else.
strings.editor/rootRedirectHint: When the app asks for a file from "/", send it back to the app instead of the ArozOS web root.
strings.editor/rewriteHint: Rewrites links in pages and style sheets and injects a small script that routes the app's own requests. Needed by most apps that were built to run at "/".
strings.editor/hostnameHint: Point this name at the same server as ArozOS (a DNS record, or a public hostname in Cloudflare Tunnel). Cloudflare's free certificate only covers one level, so prefer app.example.com or app-nas.example.com over app.nas.example.com.
strings.editor/portalHint: Where users sign in before being sent to the app.
strings.editor/ipWarning: You are using ArozOS through an IP address. Subdomain mode needs a domain name.
strings.editor/framingHint: Remove the app's "do not frame me" headers so it can open in a desktop window.
strings.editor/requireLoginHint: Turn off only for apps meant to be public, for example a status page.
strings.editor/groupsHint: None selected means every user can see it and pin it to their desktop.
strings.editor/needTrust: Tick "I trust this container" or use subdomain mode.
strings.editor/confirmRemove: Remove {name}? Desktop shortcuts to it will stop working.

strings.probe/pathRewrite: Works under a path with root path rewriting
